structure: Part 5, the overview task list and the notification actions, read eleven files of repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend in full: the hub feature folder (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, hub.fit.spec.js, 538 lines), the notification-actions feature folder (page.js, controller.js, notification-actions.fit.spec.js), and two live-animals flow files (flow/task-rows.js, flow/notification-action-slugs.js). Supporting reads for route and constant values only, not claimed beyond what the slice shows: src/server/app/shared/paths.js (hubRoutePath, pageRoutePath, pagePath, hubPath, dashboardPath), src/server/app/shared/trail.js:12-16 (TRAIL_START.overview is 'overview', so the trail parameter reads ?from=overview), src/server/app/shared/kit.js:71 (CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG is 'cancel-amend'), src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/page.js:3 (slug 'delete'), features/check-answers/page.js:3 (slug 'notification-view') and features/check-answers/controller.js:258 (its only registered route), and shared/copy.en.js:51-64 for the shared button strings the two fit specs drive. The part covers one page, the overview at GET /notifications/{journeyId} (its H1 'Overview', the 'Your commodities' totals section, the 'Notification task list' of six numbered section groups holding twelve task rows, and the Review and submit / Return to dashboard button pair), the twelve task rows' titles, hint, link targets and the two status words a row can show, every behaviour the 23 hub fit tests prove, the four notification action slugs (amend, cancel-amend, copy, delete) of which this feature registers only POST /notifications/{journeyId}/copy, that route's success, no-copy, recoverable-failure and stale-token outcomes, the four notification-actions fit tests, and Welsh key parity for the hub's copy. It stops before the confirmation pages the actions lead to (part 7), the dashboard that renders the Copy as new button, the check-answers review page, and the generic flow, gate and status layers under src/server/app/flow and src/server/app/bridge.

claims.statement: A trader reaches the live-animals notification overview at GET /notifications/{journeyId} under the set base, with the notification's own reference in the path.
claims.note: paths.js:6 is `export const hubRoutePath = () => '/notifications/{journeyId}'`.

claims.statement: The overview takes no form submission: the hub feature registers a GET route only.
claims.quote:
method: 'GET',
    path: hubRoutePath(),
claims.note: Both controls on the page are govukButton calls given an href, so they render as links styled as buttons (template.njk:43-54).

claims.statement: The overview page's heading and browser title both read "Overview".
claims.quote: title: 'Overview',
claims.note: controller.js passes `pageTitle: copy.title, heading: copy.title`, and template.njk:6 renders the heading as `<h1 class="govuk-heading-xl">`.

claims.statement: The overview page is at maturity "detailing": its behaviour has not been signed off.
claims.quote: export const hubPage = { id: 'hub', maturity: 'detailing' }

claims.statement: The overview opens with a "Your commodities" section headed at level 2.
claims.quote: heading: 'Your commodities',

<div class="govuk-grid-row">

claims.quote:
animalsLabel: 'Animals',
    animalsCaption: 'Total number of animals in this consignment',
    animalsRegionLabel: 'Animals summary',

claims.statement: The packages box reads its total, then the label "Packages/boxes", then the caption "Total number of packages in this consignment", and is announced as "Packages summary".

packagesLabel: 'Packages/boxes',

claims.statement: The animals total on the overview is the sum of every commodity line's number of animals, and the packages total the sum of every line's number of packages.
claims.note: mechanism: adds up the commodity lines' numberOfAnimalsQuantity and numberOfPackages answers for display on the overview.

claims.statement: A commodity line whose number of animals or number of packages is blank or not a number counts as zero in the overview totals rather than breaking the page.
claims.note: mechanism: coerces a commodity line's count answer to a number for the overview totals.

claims.statement: Both totals read 0 on a notification where no commodity has been added.
Each totals box reads in the order number, then label, then caption, with the "Your commodities" heading at level 2 and each box's label at level 3.
The totals boxes hold no link and no button: they report numbers and lead nowhere.
claims.quote: test('the boxes hold no link and no button', async ({ page }) => {

claims.statement: On a phone-width screen the two totals boxes stack one above the other and the overview has no horizontal overflow.
Below the commodity totals the overview shows a section headed "Notification task list" at level 2.
claims.quote: taskListHeading: 'Notification task list',

claims.statement: The task list is grouped into six numbered sections headed, in order, "1. About the consignment", "2. Description of the goods", "3. Transport and arrival", "4. Documents", "5. Addresses" and "6. Contact address", with nothing after them.
claims.quote:
groups: {
    'about-the-consignment': '1. About the consignment',
    'description-of-the-goods': '2. Description of the goods',
    'transport-and-arrival': '3. Transport and arrival',
    documents: '4. Documents',
    'consignment-parties': '5. Addresses',
    'contact-address': '6. Contact address'
  },
claims.note: The fifth group's heading is "5. Addresses" while the task row inside it is titled "Consignment addresses" (see the addresses row claim).

claims.statement: Each section heading is rendered at level 3 inside its own named region, and each region holds exactly one task list.
A journey section that owns no task row is not shown on the overview at all, which is why the start and review sections have no heading there.
claims.quote:
journeySections()
    .map((section) => ({ section, rows: taskRowsOfSection(section) }))
    .filter(({ rows }) => rows.length > 0)
claims.note: The eight journey sections live in another part's flow/journey-flow.js; the hub's own copy names only the six that carry rows.

claims.statement: The "Main import reason" task sits in the first section, "1. About the consignment".
The second section lists its tasks in the order "Commodity details", "Identification details", "Additional details".
claims.quote:
await expect(
      sectionRegion(page, 'description-of-the-goods').getByRole('link')
    ).toHaveText([
      copy.rows.consignmentDetails.title,
      copy.rows.animalIdentification.title,
      copy.rows.additionalDetails.title
    ])

claims.statement: The overview's task list holds twelve rows: origin, commodities, import reason, commodity details, identification details, additional details, arrival details, transit countries, transport details, documents, consignment addresses and contact.
claims.quote:
export const taskRows = [
  { id: 'origin', pages: [originPage] },
claims.note: The twelve row ids in task-rows.js match the twelve keys of copy.rows in the hub's copy.en.js exactly; two of them (animalIdentification, transitCountries) are conditional and may be hidden.

claims.statement: The origin task is titled "Where is this consignment coming from?".
The commodities task is titled "What are you importing?".
The import reason task is titled "Main import reason".
The commodity numbers task is titled "Commodity details".
The additional details task is titled "Additional details".
The animal identification task is titled "Identification details".
The arrival task is titled "Arrival details".
The transit countries task is titled "Transit countries".
The transporter task is titled "Transport details".
The addresses task is titled "Consignment addresses".
claims.quote:
addresses: {
      title: 'Consignment addresses',

claims.statement: The consignment addresses task carries the hint "Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination", and it is the only task on the overview with a hint.
claims.quote: hint: 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination'
claims.note: The fit test asserts the hint is the accessible description of that row's link, followed by the status word, and that every other row's link has only its status word as its accessible description.

claims.statement: The contact task is titled "Contact address for this consignment".
The documents task is titled "Upload documents".
A task on the overview shows one of exactly two status words: a green "Complete" tag or a blue "To do" tag.
claims.note: The copy file gives `complete: 'Complete'` and `toDo: 'To do'`.

claims.statement: A task reads "Complete" only when every answer it covers is given and none of its stored answers is invalid; anything else, including a part-answered or not-applicable task that is still shown, reads "To do".
claims.quote:
const statusTag = (status, invalid) =>
  status === FULFILLED && !invalid ? COMPLETE_TAG : TO_DO_TAG
claims.note: mechanism: chooses a task-list tag from the row's computed status and the set of rows whose stored answers no longer validate (invalidRowIds).

claims.statement: The overview never shows a task as unavailable: no "Cannot start yet" status is rendered, and every task shown reads Complete or To do.
claims.quote: test('leads the secondary Return to dashboard button, with no task shut as Cannot start yet', async ({

claims.statement: Every task on the overview is a link to its first open page, and that link carries the overview as the page's return trail (?from=overview).
claims.quote: const fromOverview = (href) => withTrail(href, [TRAIL_START.overview])
claims.note: shared/trail.js:12-16 gives TRAIL_START.overview the value 'overview', so the query reads ?from=overview, as the fit spec's href assertions show.

claims.statement: A conditional task is hidden from the overview when it does not apply to the notification or when none of its pages can be opened yet.
claims.quote:
const isHiddenRow = (row, status, scope) =>
  row.conditional && (status === NA || !somePageOpens(row, scope))

claims.statement: The identification details task and the transit countries task are the only conditional tasks, so they are the only two that can be absent from the overview.
claims.quote:
id: 'animalIdentification',
    pages: [animalIdentificationPage],
    parts: [{ collection: 'commodityLines', only: ['animalIdentifiers'] }],
    conditional: true,
    applies: hasAnyCommodityLine
  },
claims.note: The transit countries row is `{ id: 'transitCountries', pages: [transitCountriesPage], conditional: true }` at :64, with no `applies`, so it is hidden only while its page's gate is shut; the gate itself lives in the transport feature, another part.

claims.statement: While no commodity has been chosen the identification details task is absent from the overview, and the "2. Description of the goods" heading is still shown.
claims.quote: test('overview: when no commodity is chosen, the animal identification row is absent', async ({

claims.statement: Once a commodity that carries identifiers is chosen, the identification details task appears on the overview as a link.
claims.quote: test('overview: when a commodity carrying identifiers is chosen, the animal identification row appears', async ({

claims.quote: test('renders navigation copy and the task statuses of a newly entered journey', async ({
claims.note: The same test asserts the Overview heading and all six section headings are visible.

claims.quote:

    ]

claims.statement: The commodity details task links to the consignment-details page, and while no commodity is chosen opening it leads the trader to the "What are you importing?" question instead.
Opening the arrival details task from the overview with only the country of origin answered shows the port of entry question, and saving it leads on to the commodity search.
claims.quote: test('saving arrival details with only the country of origin answered opens What are you importing?', async ({

claims.statement: Leaving a question page with "Cancel and return to overview" returns the trader to the overview with the answers unsaved, so the commodity details task still reads "To do" while the commodities task reads "Complete".
claims.quote:
await page
    .getByRole('link', { name: sharedCopy.saveActions.cancelAndReturnToHub })
    .click()
  await expectHub(page)
claims.note: shared/copy.en.js:64 gives cancelAndReturnToHub the words 'Cancel and return to overview'.

claims.statement: Saving a question page with "Save and return to overview" returns the trader to the overview, and the task whose answers were saved then reads "Complete" while the other tasks keep their statuses.
claims.quote: test('reads Complete once the numbers are saved, leaving the other rows alone', async ({
claims.note: shared/copy.en.js:63 gives saveAndReturnToHub the words 'Save and return to overview'.

claims.statement: A task's completeness is measured over the answers assigned to it, so the commodities task ignores each commodity line's identifiers, number of animals and number of packages.
The commodity details task is complete when every commodity line has its number of animals and number of packages, and nothing else.
The identification details task is complete when every commodity line has its animal identifiers, and it does not apply at all while the notification has no commodity line.
claims.quote:
parts: [{ collection: 'commodityLines', only: ['animalIdentifiers'] }],
    conditional: true,
    applies: hasAnyCommodityLine

claims.statement: A single-species notification can reach the review with no animal identifier saved, and its identification details task still reads "Complete".
claims.quote: test('a single-species notification reaches the review with no identifier saved', async ({

claims.statement: The consignment addresses task covers two pages, the addresses page and the CPH number page, and stays short of complete until every addressable animal has a permanent address even when both pages' answers are given.
claims.quote:
id: 'addresses',
    pages: [addressesPage, cphNumberPage],
    extraAnswerGiven: everyAddressableAnimalHasPermanentAddress
claims.note: rowStatus turns a fulfilled row whose extraAnswerGiven is false into IN_PROGRESS, which the hub renders as the "To do" tag.

claims.statement: A task that does not apply to the notification is reported as not applicable rather than as part-answered, which is what lets a conditional task be hidden.
claims.note: mechanism: computes a task row's status from its assigned answers, the notification's scope and the obligation evaluation.

claims.statement: The overview ends with two buttons in order: a primary "Review and submit" and a secondary "Return to dashboard".
claims.quote:
reviewAndSubmit: 'Review and submit',
  returnToDashboard: 'Return to dashboard',
claims.note: The fit test also measures the first against the GOV.UK primary button style and the second against govuk-button--secondary.

claims.statement: "Review and submit" leads to the notification view at /notifications/{journeyId}/notification-view?from=overview.
claims.quote:
const reviewHref = (journeyId) =>
  fromOverview(pagePath(journeyId, notificationViewPage.slug))
claims.note: The fit test asserts the href matches /\/notifications\/[^/]+\/notification-view\?from=overview$/.

claims.statement: "Review and submit" opens the review whatever state the notification is in: with only the country of origin answered it reaches the draft review, and it does so again once every answer section is complete.
claims.quote: test('opens the review from a notification with only the origin answered', async ({

claims.statement: The overview shows nothing to say a notification is ready to review: there is no readiness banner, no progress count and no change to the Review and submit button when every task reads Complete.
claims.note: Looked in the hub template (which renders only the heading, the totals section, the task list and the two buttons), in the handler's view model (pageTitle, heading, copy, sharedCopy, journeyStrip, commodityTotals, groups, reviewHref, dashboardHref) and in the hub copy file; none holds a readiness state. The review page's own gate, readyForCheckYourAnswers, sits in another part's flow.

claims.statement: "Return to dashboard" leads to the set's own notification list at the set base, and clicking it takes the trader there.
claims.quote: dashboardHref: dashboardPath()
claims.note: shared/paths.js:15 gives `dashboardPath = () => setBase()`; the fit test asserts the button's href is the set base and that clicking it lands there.

claims.statement: The overview has no back link.
claims.quote: await expect(backLink(page)).toHaveCount(0)

claims.statement: The overview shows the shared journey strip for the notification, so its reference and status are on the page.
claims.quote: journeyStrip: journeyStrip(journey),
claims.note: The template extends shared/layout.njk, which renders the strip; the strip's own copy ('Draft', 'Submitted' and the rest) belongs to the shared layout part. The notification-actions fit spec reads 'Draft' off a copied notification's overview.

claims.statement: The overview has no serious or critical accessibility violations, whether nothing but the origin is answered, the notification is part complete, or the commodity totals are showing.
claims.quote: await expectNoSeriousOrCriticalViolations(page, 'Hub with commodity totals')

claims.statement: Four actions can be taken on a live-animals notification from outside the question pages: amend, cancel amend, copy and delete, reached at the slugs amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete.
claims.note: shared/kit.js:71 gives CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG the value 'cancel-amend' and delete-notification/page.js:3 the slug 'delete'.

claims.statement: Of those four actions the notification-actions feature itself serves only copy, as a POST to /notifications/{journeyId}/copy.
claims.note: Amend, cancel amend and delete are served by their own features, which other parts cover.

claims.statement: The notification-actions page is at maturity "detailing": its behaviour has not been signed off.
Copying a notification succeeds by taking the trader straight to the new draft's overview.
claims.quote:
return copied
      ? h.redirect(hubPath(copied.journeyId))
      : h.redirect(dashboardPath())

claims.statement: A copy that produces no new notification sends the trader back to the notification list rather than showing an error.
claims.quote: : h.redirect(dashboardPath())
claims.note: The branch is reached when copyJourney returns nothing; nothing is logged on it.

claims.statement: A copy request carries where it was started from, and the service distinguishes a copy started on the notification view from one started on the notification list.
claims.quote:
const originPath = (request) =>
  request.payload?.copyOrigin === 'notification-view'
    ? pagePath(request.params.journeyId, 'check-answers')
    : dashboardPath()
claims.note: mechanism: reads the posted copyOrigin field to pick where a refused or failed copy returns the trader.

claims.statement: When a copy cannot be saved, the trader is shown the page they started from again, carrying a recoverable-error message, with an HTTP 500 status: the notification view if the copy was started there, otherwise the notification list.
claims.quote:
const recoverCopy = (request, h) =>
  request.payload?.copyOrigin === 'notification-view'
    ? renderNotificationView(request, h, { recoverableError: true })
    : renderDashboard(request, h, { recoverableError: true })

claims.statement: A copy posted against a notification that has moved on since the page was loaded is refused, and the trader is returned to where they started with a stale-action marker in the URL (?staleAction=1).
claims.note: The refusal is logged once at info with the notification's id and the reason.

claims.statement: A copy refused as stale that was started on the notification view sends the trader to /notifications/{journeyId}/check-answers, a path the service serves no page at, so the refusal does not land on the review page it means to.
claims.quote: ? pagePath(request.params.journeyId, 'check-answers')
claims.note: 'check-answers' appears as a path nowhere else in src/server: the review page's slug is 'notification-view' (features/check-answers/page.js:3) and its only route comes from pageRoutes(page, ...) at features/check-answers/controller.js:258. The copy handler's own success and failure paths use the page objects' slugs rather than this literal.

claims.statement: A copy request carries the version of the notification it was started from, so a trader's copy can be checked against the record's current version.
claims.quote:
const concurrencyToken =
    request.payload?.concurrencyToken != null
      ? Number(request.payload.concurrencyToken)
      : undefined
claims.note: mechanism: reads the posted concurrencyToken field and passes it as a number to copyJourney; a request without one passes nothing.

claims.statement: A trader copies a notification from the notification list with a button reading "Copy as new" that also names the notification's reference for a screen reader.
claims.note: shared/copy.en.js:52-54 gives the copy action the words 'Copy as new'; the hidden reference text belongs to the dashboard feature, another part.

claims.statement: Copying a notification creates a separate draft: the trader lands on an overview whose reference differs from the source's, and the notification shows as Draft.
claims.quote: test('copy creates a separate draft notification', async ({ page }) => {

claims.statement: The copy keeps the source notification's answers: the new draft's origin task reads Complete and holds the same country of origin.
After a copy both the source notification and the copy are listed, each under its own reference.
claims.quote: test('copy leaves both source and copied notifications on the dashboard', async ({

claims.statement: A copied notification's overview has no serious or critical accessibility violations.
claims.quote: test('copied notification hub has no serious or critical axe violations', async ({

claims.statement: Nothing in the notification-actions feature proves what amend, cancel amend or delete do: its only tests are the four copy tests.
claims.note: Looked at every test in the feature's fit spec (copy creates a separate draft, copy preserves the source answers, copy leaves both on the dashboard, copied hub axe) and at its controller, which registers the copy route alone. The other three slugs' behaviour sits in the amend, cancel-amend and delete features, which other parts cover.

claims.statement: The overview carries no caption above its heading: the page opens straight on the "Overview" H1.
claims.quote:
{% block journeyContent %}

{{ heading }}
claims.note: Looked at the hub template's journeyContent block (nothing before the H1), the handler's view model (no caption key, controller.js:120-130), the hub copy file (no caption key) and shared/layout.njk (which holds no caption). The set's question pages take a section caption from the journey flow, which is another part.

claims.statement: A trader starting a live-animals notification lands on the overview, and every journey page's Save or Cancel and return action brings them back to it.
claims.quote:
const expectHub = (page) =>
  expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: copy.title })).toBeVisible()
claims.note: Every test in the hub fit spec opens with startNotification(page) and then finds the Overview heading; the copy action lands there too (notification-actions.fit.spec.js:39-41).

claims.statement: The overview is offered in Welsh with every English key translated: the Welsh copy carries the same key tree as the English, with no key missing and none extra.
claims.quote: title: 'Trosolwg',
claims.note: Both files hold title, commodityTotals (heading, animalsLabel, animalsCaption, animalsRegionLabel, packagesLabel, packagesCaption, packagesRegionLabel), reviewAndSubmit, returnToDashboard, statuses (complete, toDo), taskListHeading, groups (the six section ids) and rows (the twelve row ids, with hint only under addresses). The Welsh file is headed 'MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator. Do not ship user-facing without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.'
